Definition: middle voice from an apparently primary ὦνος (a sum or price); to purchase (synonymous with the earlier G4092):-- buy.
BiblicalUsage: Oneomai means to buy, to purchase for a sum. It occurs once, in Acts 7:16, where the patriarchs are carried over into Sychem and laid in the sepulchre Abraham bought for a sum of money of the sons of Emmor.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the bought grave is the first ground Abraham owned in the promise, and the purchase proves the promise was real.
